instructions.name: add_liquidity
docs: Add proportional liquidity to a seeded pool and mint LP to the user.
Rejects an unseeded pool with `PoolNotSeeded` (see `seed_liquidity`).
# Parameters
* `token_amounts`     — per-token deposit ceilings in pool order.
* `minimum_lp_amount`— slippage floor on LP received.
# Used by
User wallets, single-token-liquidity helper.

accounts.name: token_program
docs: Token program for the LP mint (same one used for `lp_mint`).
Per-token programs come via `remaining_accounts` because each
pool token may use a different program.

instructions.name: cancel_pool_action
docs: Clear pending slot `kind` (0 = admin transfer … 10 = token
re-enable). `NoPendingAction` when empty.
# Authority
`pool.pool_admin`.

instructions.name: cancel_pool_admin_transfer
docs: Cancel a pending pool-admin transfer.

instructions.name: cancel_protocol_admin_transfer
docs: Cancel a pending protocol-admin transfer.

instructions.name: claim_creator_fees
docs: Sweep `pool.creator_fees_owed` (v6.1 T14) for every token to
caller-supplied recipients and zero the counters. Pool-admin only,
any time, no cooldown; a call with nothing owed is a no-op that
still emits `CreatorFeesClaimed` with zero amounts. Never touches
`actual_balance` or `protocol_fees_owed`.
# remaining_accounts
`[vault_i, recipient_i, mint_i, token_program_i]` per token, plus
an optional tail of transfer-hook / memo accounts — the same layout
as `collect_protocol_fees`.
# Used by
The pool admin's wallet (`scripts/cli/claim-creator-fees.ts`,
`admin-panel/17-claim-creator-fees.ts`), frontend claim button.

instructions.name: collect_protocol_fees
docs: Sweep `protocol_fees_owed` for every token to caller-supplied
recipients and zero the counters.
# Authority
`protocol_admin` AND Treasury PDA.
# remaining_accounts
`[vault_i, recipient_i, mint_i, token_program_i]` per token, plus
an optional tail of transfer-hook / memo accounts.
# Used by
`protocol_admin::pool_collect_protocol_fees` (CPI).

instructions.name: debug_withdraw_liquidity
docs: Emergency drain — pool becomes BRICKED.
`actual_balances` and `virtual_balances` are intentionally NOT
updated. Once vaults are drained out-of-band the pool's bookkeeping
is meaningless, so the pool MUST stay `pool_enabled = false`
forever. Re-enabling would let users swap/join against stale
state and extract value at LP / protocol expense.
# Authority
`protocol_admin` AND Treasury PDA.
# Prerequisites
`pool.pool_enabled == false` (handler enforces).
# Parameters
* `token_amounts` — per-token withdraw amounts (use 0 to skip).
# remaining_accounts
`[vault_i, recipient_i, mint_i, token_program_i]` per token, plus
an optional tail of transfer-hook / memo accounts.
# Used by
`protocol_admin::pool_debug_withdraw_liquidity` (CPI),
driven by `admin-panel/03-emergency-withdraw.ts`.

instructions.name: disable_pool_admin
docs: Permanently renounce pool-admin on this pool. Single-step,
irreversible. v6.1 (T14): refused with `CreatorFeesUnclaimed` while
any `creator_fees_owed` slot is non-zero (claim first), and clears
`creator_fee_bps` to 0 — with no admin there is no recipient, so
the LPs keep the whole LP share from then on.

instructions.name: execute_lock_liquidity_fees
docs: Execute the pending `LockLiquidityFees` (kind 5).

instructions.name: execute_lock_range_manager
docs: Execute the pending `LockRangeManager` (kind 6);
`RangeManagerMustBeUnset` if a manager was appointed in the meantime.

instructions.name: execute_set_creator_fee_bps
docs: Execute the pending `SetCreatorFeeBps` (kind 3).

instructions.name: execute_set_delay
docs: Execute the pending `SetDelay` (kind 1) once `eta <= now <= eta +
14 d`; live slots are pushed to `max(eta, now + new)` when the delay
rises. Every `execute_*` below clears its slot first, then applies
the change through the same code path as the direct instruction (all
preconditions re-checked) and emits `PoolActionExecuted`.

instructions.name: execute_set_liquidity_fees
docs: Execute the pending `SetLiquidityFees` (kind 4); `LiquidityFeesLocked`
if the fees were locked in the meantime.

instructions.name: execute_set_max_selloff
docs: Execute the pending `SetMaxSelloff` (kind 9). `params` must be the
proposed vector (`PendingPayloadMismatch` otherwise) and is validated
again.

instructions.name: execute_set_range_manager
docs: Execute the pending `SetRangeManager` (kind 7); `RangeManagerLocked`
if the pool was locked in the meantime.

instructions.name: execute_set_range_manager_config
docs: Execute the pending `SetRangeManagerConfig` (kind 8).

instructions.name: execute_set_swap_fee_rate
docs: Execute the pending `SetSwapFeeRate` (kind 2).

instructions.name: execute_set_token_active
docs: Execute the pending `SetTokenActive` (kind 10): re-enables the
proposed token index.

instructions.name: fund_sidelined_token
docs: Fund a sidelined slot (`actual_balance == 0`) of a seeded pool at its
current virtual price. Pool-admin only; mints no LP (the reserves
accrue to every LP holder); virtual balances are untouched.
# Parameters
* `token_index` — slot to fund, `< pool.token_count`.
* `amount`      — gross amount transferred (raw units); the NET
amount after any Token-2022 transfer fee is booked.
# remaining_accounts
Optional Token-2022 hook / memo tail only.
# Used by
Pool admins (admin panel, SDK `buildFundSidelinedTokenIx`).

accounts.name: lp_mint
docs: Read-only: its `supply` is the "pool is seeded" signal.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Must equal `pool.pool_admin` (checked in the handler, after the
renounced-admin check, so a renounced pool reports
`PoolAdminDisabled` instead of an unreachable `Unauthorized`).

accounts.name: user_token
docs: owned by `token_program`, mint == pool token, owner == `authority`.

accounts.name: mint
docs: re-asserted against the FIX-6 pin.

instructions.name: get_pool_info
docs: Read-only "view": emit a `PoolInfo` event with the pool's full
state. Intended for `simulate({ commitment: ... })` calls; not
useful as part of a signed transaction.
# Used by
SDK helpers, frontend pool-detail pages, indexer health-check
fallback.

instructions.name: initialize_config
docs: Initialise a new `CofferPoolConfig`. Treasury wrapper passes the
Treasury PDA as both admin pubkeys; direct calls produce
Initialise a fresh `CofferPoolConfig`.
# Parameters
* `protocol_admin`           — pubkey allowed to pause pools, set
`protocol_fee_rate`, collect fees, drain via debug-withdraw,
and rotate itself via the pending/accept flow.
* `default_protocol_fee_rate`— stored on the config (basis points,
≤ `MAX_PROTOCOL_FEE_RATE`); informational since v6.1 (T15) — new
pools start at the constant `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_FEE_RATE` (10%).
Pool-admin (level-1) is per-pool — set automatically to the wallet
that calls `initialize_pool`.

accounts.name: protocol_admin_treasury
docs: Treasury PDA of the protocol-admin program. Validated two ways:
the `seeds` + `seeds::program` constraint pins *which* account this
must be, and the `Signer` type proves the call came through
protocol-admin's admin-gated CPI (only that program can
`invoke_signed` these seeds).
The type must be `Signer` rather than an `UncheckedAccount` with an
`is_signer` constraint: Anchor derives CPI account metas from the
field TYPE, so an `UncheckedAccount` here would be emitted with
`is_signer: false` and the caller's `invoke_signed` signature would
never reach this program.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the rent for `config`. Must be a `Signer`.

instructions.name: initialize_pool
docs: Initialise a fresh pool under `config`. Creates the pool PDA and
LP mint, validates token mints / weights / virtual balances, and
pins per-token programs.
The pool's token set is the `remaining_accounts` list — one mint per
token, in the same order as the weights. There is no `tokens` argument:
it duplicated those accounts exactly and cost 324 bytes at 10 tokens,
which alone pushed a 10-token deploy past the transaction size limit.
# Parameters
* `normalized_weights`       — basis points, sum = `WEIGHT_SCALE`.
* `initial_virtual_balances` — seed virtual balances (raw units),
each > 0.
* `swap_fee_rate`            — hundredths of bps,
≤ `MAX_SWAP_FEE_RATE`.
* `pool_id`                  — caller-chosen 64-bit salt baked
into PDA seeds. Unique per config.
* `creator_fee_bps`          — v6.1 (T14) pool admin's share of the
LP fee remainder, `0..=MAX_CREATOR_FEE_BPS`; `0` = off (default).
No extension-policy argument (removed in v6.1, T19): admission is
structural only, see `util::token::validate_mint_for_admission`.
`lp_metadata` (v6.1, T1): immutable LP token name / symbol / uri,
written into the Token-2022 LP mint in this same instruction. There
is no update instruction, by design.
`deposit_fee_bps` / `withdraw_fee_bps` (v6.1, T7): liquidity fees in
basis points, `0..=10_000` each; born unlocked (`lock_liquidity_fees`).
`hook_config` (v6.1, T9): optional, immutable native hook (`None` =
no hook). The hook's `on-register` callback runs inside this
instruction and may refuse the pool; its declared flags must equal
`hook_config.flags`. See `hooks` and `coffer_hook_interface`.
# remaining_accounts
One mint account per token in `tokens` order, then — iff
`hook_config` is `Some` — the `hook_config.accounts_len` accounts of
the hook slice `[hook_program, hook_caller, extras..]` (the mint count
is `remaining.len() − accounts_len`).
# Used by
SDK `PoolFactoryClient.buildDeployPoolTx`, deploy-pool scripts.

accounts.name: config
docs: Parent governance config. Read-only — only its pubkey is consumed
(v6.1 T15: the protocol fee rate is `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_FEE_RATE`,
not `config.default_protocol_fee_rate`).

accounts.name: pool
docs: New pool PDA. Seeded so multiple pools per config are possible
via distinct `pool_id` values.

accounts.name: lp_mint
docs: Brand-new Token-2022 LP mint. Authority is the pool PDA, decimals
fixed at `LP_DECIMALS` (= 9), no freeze authority. Anchor allocates
the base mint + `MetadataPointer` (234 bytes); the handler grows it
to the exact `TokenMetadata` size. `metadata_address = lp_mint` and
no `::authority` ⇒ the pointer can never be re-targeted.

accounts.name: lp_token_program
docs: Pinned to Token-2022: the only program that can hold in-mint
metadata, and the only `invoke_signed` target (besides System) the
pool PDA signs for in this instruction.

instructions.name: initialize_pool_alt
docs: Provision a per-pool Address Lookup Table so client SDKs can build
`VersionedTransaction`s for `add_liquidity` / `remove_liquidity` on
pools whose account count exceeds the legacy 1232-byte ceiling
(≥ 7 tokens in practice).
# Parameters
* `recent_slot` — recent slot used by the ALT program to derive
the table address. Caller should pass
`connection.getSlot('finalized')`.
# Flow
One transaction performs three CPIs into the ALT program:
`create_lookup_table` → `extend_lookup_table` (pool, LP mint,
vaults, mints, standard programs) → `freeze_lookup_table`.
The ALT becomes immutable forever — its rent (~0.005 SOL for a
7-token pool) is permanently locked.
# Authority
`pool.pool_admin`. Idempotent: rejects with `AltAlreadyInitialized`
if `pool.lookup_table != Pubkey::default()`.
# Used by
`scripts/cli/initialize-pool-alts.ts` (one-shot bootstrap for
existing prod pools), and `sdk` after `initialize_pool` on
fresh pools.

accounts.name: pool
docs: Pool to provision the ALT for. Must have `lookup_table ==
Pubkey::default()`. The handler writes the new ALT address back
onto this account.

accounts.name: config
docs: `CofferPoolConfig` this pool inherits governance from. Pinned via
`pool.config`. Reading it lets the handler also accept
`config.protocol_admin` as an authority — which is the Treasury
PDA, only signable through `protocol_admin.pool_initialize_alt`.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Authority. Must equal either `pool.pool_admin` (per-pool owner
path) or `config.protocol_admin` (Treasury PDA via the
protocol-admin CPI wrapper). Authorises the ALT creation; the
derived ALT address is `[authority, recent_slot]`.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Payer for ALT rent + per-extend top-ups. Decoupled from
`authority` because Treasury PDA (the wrapper-path authority)
owns data and so cannot be `from` in `system_program::transfer`.
In the pool-admin path callers pass the same key for both — no
behavioural change.

accounts.name: lookup_table
docs: `[authority, recent_slot]` by the ALT program. Re-derived and
matched against this account in the handler.

accounts.name: alt_program
docs: `solana_address_lookup_table_interface::id()` in the handler.

instructions.name: initiate_pool_admin_transfer
docs: Step 1 — current `pool.pool_admin` proposes a successor.

instructions.name: initiate_protocol_admin_transfer
docs: Step 1 — current `config.protocol_admin` proposes a successor.

instructions.name: lock_liquidity_fees
docs: Freeze the liquidity fees at their current values for ever (v6.1,
T7). One-way: no instruction clears the lock; a second call fails
with `LiquidityFeesAlreadyLocked`. Survives admin rotation and
`disable_pool_admin`. The anti-rug guarantee LPs can check before
depositing.
# Authority
`pool_admin`.

instructions.name: lock_range_manager
docs: Permanently forbid a range manager on this pool (v6.1, T6). One-way:
sets `pool.range_manager_locked`; nothing clears it. Requires the
manager to be unset (`range_manager == default`, `!enabled`) so a bot
can never be frozen in place. Afterwards `set_range_manager` (any
caller), `set_range_manager_config` and `range_manager_update` fail
with `RangeManagerLocked`; swaps, liquidity, fees and the pool-admin
handshake are unaffected. Works on paused pools.
# Authority
`pool.pool_admin` only.
# Errors
`PoolAdminDisabled`, `Unauthorized`, `RangeManagerLocked`,
`RangeManagerMustBeUnset`.

instructions.name: migrate_pool_layout_v61
docs: Grow a 1683-byte v4/v5 pool account in place to `CofferPool::LEN`
(2304 bytes). **Permissionless, one-shot, no semantic change**: the
legacy bytes are untouched, the appended block gets
`layout_version = 1` and the FIX-6 `token_decimals` pins (read from
the mints passed as `remaining_accounts`, each pinned to its slot),
`reserved_v61` is zero. `payer` funds the rent delta.
Until a pool has been migrated every other instruction that reads it
(in coffer-pool, protocol-admin and STLD) fails with
`LayoutVersionMismatch`; SDKs key on that code to prepend this
instruction. Works on frozen pools and on pools that have not run
`migrate_to_v5` yet (run this first, then `migrate_to_v5`).
# remaining_accounts
One mint account per pool token, in slot order.
# Errors
`AlreadyMigrated` when the pool is already 2304 bytes (idempotency).
# Used by
`scripts/cli/migrate-pool-layout-v61.ts` (rollout), SDK tx builders.

accounts.name: pool
docs: 1683-byte account this instruction exists to convert. Owner is pinned
here; discriminator, exact legacy length and token count are checked
in the handler before any write.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Funds the rent delta for the extra bytes. Anyone.

instructions.name: migrate_to_v5
docs: Pool storage migration entrypoint for the v4 → v5 layout change.
**This instruction mutates state — it is not a no-op.** When
`reactivate_tokens` is set it flips every token's `is_active` back to
`true` and writes the migration marker. Since v6.1 (T19) it no longer
backfills any extension policy; the former bitmap slot is deprecated.
# Parameters
* `reactivate_tokens` — pass `true` ONLY on the one-shot v4 → v5 pass,
where `is_active` decodes as `false` because it lands on the old
zeroed `reserved` byte. Pass `false` on every later call: `true`
would silently re-open every token an admin deliberately disabled
with `set_token_active(i, false)`.
# Authority
`pool.pool_admin` OR `config.protocol_admin`, neither being the
default key.
Idempotent in both directions — a second run backfills nothing and
reactivates nothing.

accounts.name: config
docs: Parent config — authorises via `protocol_admin`.

instructions.name: propose_pool_action
docs: Queue a D-class pool-admin action: validated like the direct
instruction, stored in its typed `pending_*` slot with
`eta = now + pool_admin_delay_secs` (`SetDelay`: `now + max(old,
new)`). Re-proposing a kind overwrites its slot. Emits
`PoolActionProposed { kind, payload: borsh(action), eta }`.
# Authority
`pool.pool_admin`.

instructions.name: range_manager_update
docs: Tweak any subset of `virtual_balances` and / or `normalized_weights`
within the configured envelope. Range-manager only.
# Parameters
* `vb_changes`     — sparse `[(index, new_vb)]`; may be empty.
* `weight_changes` — sparse `[(index, new_weight_bps)]`; may be
empty. The resulting weight vector must sum to `WEIGHT_SCALE`
and stay within `[MIN_WEIGHT, MAX_WEIGHT]` per token, otherwise
the whole instruction reverts.

accounts.name: pool
docs: Mutated — handler writes new virtual_balances / normalized_weights
and bumps `range_manager_last_updated`.
`pool_enabled` is part of the gate: swaps and liquidity operations
honour the kill switch, and a range manager that kept rewriting
virtual balances and weights through a protocol-level pause would
leave governance with no way to contain a misbehaving one (only the
pool admin can un-appoint it).

instructions.name: remove_liquidity
docs: Burn LP proportionally and pay out tokens.
# Minimum-supply floor
The pool always retains at least `MIN_LP_SUPPLY` of supply
so the proportional math never sees a zero-supply state. If the
caller's `lp_amount` would push supply below the floor, the burn
is silently capped at `total_supply - MIN_LP_SUPPLY` and
the residual LP stays in the user's wallet.
# Parameters
* `lp_amount`            — caller's requested burn (raw LP).
* `minimum_token_amounts` — per-token slippage floors against the
*effective* (capped) burn.
# Used by
User wallets, SDK `LiquidityClient`.

instructions.name: remove_liquidity_bypass_hooks
docs: `remove_liquidity` WITHOUT the hook callbacks (v6.1, T9): the same
accounts, arguments, math, exit fee (T7) and surge-bucket payout
(T12) — byte-identical economics — but the pool's hook is never
CPI'd and the remaining-accounts tail carries NO hook slice (only the
optional Token-2022 tail). Always available, on every pool, with no
admin gate: an LP can always exit, whatever the hook program does
(reverts, burns CU, was closed, was upgraded). Emits the same events
minus `HookInvoked`.
# Used by
SDK `LiquidityClient` fallback, frontend "exit without hook" path.

instructions.name: rescale_virtual_balances
docs: v6.1 (T22): price-neutral repair of a pool that violates the strict
leverage invariant (`virtual_balance > actual_balance` on every slot,
e.g. a migrated legacy pool at `V == A`): multiply EVERY slot's
virtual balance by `multiplier` (`>= 2`, checked `u64`), rescale the
sell-off windows, then require the invariant and the per-slot floor
(`min_virtual_balance`) on the result. Pair prices `V_i : V_j` are
unchanged; only depth / leverage grows. Allowed on a disabled pool so
the repair can precede the unfreeze.
# Authority
`config.protocol_admin` (= Treasury PDA) — reached through
`protocol_admin::pool_rescale_virtual_balances` (D-class: queued
under the Treasury cooldown when a delay is in force).
# Errors
`InvalidVirtualRescale`, `MathOverflow`, `VirtualBalanceNotAboveActual`,
`VirtualBalanceBelowFloor`, `Unauthorized`.

instructions.name: seed_liquidity
docs: Seed the pool's first liquidity and mint a creator-chosen LP
supply. Pool-admin only; exactly once per pool
(`lp_mint.supply == 0`). Sets the LP token's price:
`Σ seed value / lp_amount`.
# Parameters
* `token_amounts` — per-token seed amounts in pool order; at least
one must be > 0 (zero slots start sidelined).
* `lp_amount`     — initial LP supply in raw units (9 decimals),
`MIN_INITIAL_LP_SUPPLY ≤ lp_amount ≤ MAX_INITIAL_LP_SUPPLY`.
# remaining_accounts
Same ×4 layout as `add_liquidity` plus the optional hook/memo tail.
# Used by
Pool creators (SDK `buildSeedLiquidityIx`, one-signature deploy).

accounts.name: user
docs: Must equal `pool.pool_admin` (checked in the handler so the error is
`SeedDepositNotPoolAdmin`, the code clients already map for H-03).

accounts.name: token_program
docs: Token program for the LP mint (same one used for `lp_mint`).

instructions.name: set_creator_fee_bps
docs: Set `pool.creator_fee_bps` — the pool admin's ("creator's")
management fee as a share of the LP remainder of every swap fee AND
surge fee (v6.1 T14, `math::fee_split`: protocol ceil first, then
this share floor of what is left, LPs the rest). Any value in
`0..=MAX_CREATOR_FEE_BPS` (100% ⇒ LPs earn nothing from fees; the
frontend discloses). Takes effect from the next swap; never
retroactive. Plain instruction: T3 wraps it in the pool-admin
cooldown queue.
# Authority
`pool_admin` only (no protocol-admin wrapper, like `set_swap_fee_rate`).
# Parameters
* `creator_fee_bps` — basis points, ≤ `MAX_CREATOR_FEE_BPS`.
# Used by
The pool admin's wallet (`scripts/cli/set-creator-fee.ts`,
`admin-panel/17-set-creator-fee.ts`), SDK.

instructions.name: set_hook_disabled
docs: Emergency switch for a pool's native hook (v6.1, T9). `true` ⇒ no
callback is invoked: swaps / deposits proceed with the base fee, or —
if the pool was created with `PAUSE_WHEN_DISABLED` — fail with
`HookPaused`; removes always proceed. `false` re-enables. While
disabled, clients omit the hook slice from the tail. Instant, no
cooldown (security action; T3 must not wrap it in the delay queue).
The hook config itself is immutable — there is no setter to gate.
# Authority
`protocol_admin` AND Treasury PDA (`protocol_admin::pool_set_hook_disabled`).
# Errors
`HookInvalidConfig` when the pool has no hook; `Unauthorized`.

instructions.name: set_liquidity_fees
docs: Set `pool.deposit_fee_bps` / `pool.withdraw_fee_bps` (v6.1, T7):
the LP haircut on `add_liquidity` and the payout haircut on
`remove_liquidity`, both retained for the remaining LPs. Rejected
for ever once `lock_liquidity_fees` ran (`LiquidityFeesLocked`).
Plain instruction: T3 wraps it in the pool-admin cooldown queue.
# Authority
`pool_admin` (no Treasury wrapper, like `set_swap_fee_rate`).
# Parameters
* `deposit_fee_bps`  — basis points, ≤ `MAX_LIQUIDITY_FEE_BPS` (100%).
* `withdraw_fee_bps` — basis points, ≤ `MAX_LIQUIDITY_FEE_BPS` (100%).

instructions.name: set_max_selloff
docs: Set the per-token sell-off policy — sliding-window cap, period, and
the variable surge-fee curve — for every active token in one call.
Pool-admin only.
# Parameters
* `params` — length == `token_count`, one
`instructions::set_max_selloff::SelloffParams` per token
(`max_selloff_pct`, `period_length`, `fee_threshold_pct`,
`fee_slope_low_pct`, `fee_slope_high_pct`; all `_pct` in
`PERCENT_SCALE` units). The surge fee rises convexly as the
window fills and is charged on the output token, 100% to the
protocol bucket.

instructions.name: set_pool_admin_delay
docs: Set `pool.pool_admin_delay_secs` directly. Allowed only while the
delay is 0 (bootstrap: raising from 0 is instant); afterwards every
change goes through `propose_pool_action(SetDelay)` and waits
`max(old, new)`. `0..=MAX_DELAY_SECS` (30 d). While a delay is in
force every D-class pool-admin instruction (fees, locks, range
manager, max-selloff, token re-enable, admin transfer) fails with
`CooldownRequired` and must be queued; emergency actions
(`set_swaps_enabled`, `set_token_active(i, false)`,
`set_range_manager(current, false)`) stay instant.
# Authority
`pool.pool_admin`.

instructions.name: set_pool_enabled
docs: Master pool kill-switch. When `enabled = false`, swaps and
add/remove liquidity all revert.
# Authority
`protocol_admin` AND Treasury PDA.
# Used by
`protocol_admin::pool_set_pool_enabled` (CPI).

instructions.name: set_protocol_fee_rate
docs: Set `pool.protocol_fee_rate` — the protocol's share of the swap fee
AND of the sell-off surge fee (v6.1 T15, `math::fee_split`). Any
value in `0..=MAX_PROTOCOL_FEE_RATE` (100%), on any decodable pool
(fresh or migrated), disabled or not. Takes effect for the next swap;
never retroactive (`protocol_fees_owed` is untouched). Plain
instruction: T3 wraps it in the admin cooldown queue.
# Authority
`protocol_admin` AND Treasury PDA.
# Parameters
* `protocol_fee_rate` — basis points, ≤ `MAX_PROTOCOL_FEE_RATE`.
# Used by
`protocol_admin::pool_set_protocol_fee_rate` (CPI).

instructions.name: set_range_manager
docs: Set or disable the range-manager pubkey on `pool`. Pool-admin only —
protocol-admin cannot reach this. Combine `new_manager =
Pubkey::default()` with `enabled = false` for the fully-disabled
state. New pools deploy with this off by default.
# Parameters
* `new_manager` — pubkey allowed to call `range_manager_update`.
* `enabled`     — gate flag; `false` blocks the manager even if
pubkey is set.

instructions.name: set_range_manager_config
docs: Configure the envelope the range-manager must stay within. Pool-
admin only. Limits are per-token (applied independently in the
update loop) and a percentage of the CURRENT value, in
`PERCENT_SCALE` units (10_000 = 100%).
# Parameters
* `max_weight_change_pct`    — ≤ 10_000.
* `min_update_interval_secs` — rate-limit between successive
`range_manager_update` calls.
* `max_leverage_bps`         — absolute band on
`virtual_balance / actual_balance` the manager must leave every
live token inside (10_000 = 1.0×; `0` disables that side). The
percentage caps above bound how FAST the manager may move; this
bounds how FAR.
* `min_leverage_bps` — the FLOOR of the same envelope, and the side
that actually protects capital. Output is priced off virtual
balances, so depressing one makes the pool believe it holds less than
it does and sells the other side's real reserves at a fabricated
rate. A ceiling alone never sees that coming. `0` disables it.
Appended at the END of the argument list — Borsh is positional.

instructions.name: set_swap_fee_rate
docs: Set `pool.swap_fee_rate`.
# Authority
`pool_admin` AND Treasury PDA.
# Parameters
* `swap_fee_rate` — hundredths of bps, ≤ `MAX_SWAP_FEE_RATE`.
# Used by
The pool admin's own wallet, and the admin panel. There is deliberately
NO `protocol_admin::pool_set_swap_fee_rate` wrapper: the swap fee is the
pool admin's parameter, not governance's, and the context requires the
pool admin to sign. Governance's lever over a pool's economics is
`pool_set_protocol_fee_rate`, which is a different field.

accounts.name: pool
docs: Mutated. `authority` must equal `pool.pool_admin` (storage-only
admin pubkey; no hardcoded address).

instructions.name: set_swaps_enabled
docs: Per-pool swap toggle (less invasive than `set_pool_enabled` —
LPs can still add/remove liquidity).
v6.1 (T8): also the creator's launch gate. Compose
`set_swaps_enabled(false)` into the deploy transaction after
`seed_liquidity` for a paused launch; `set_swaps_enabled(true)` opens
trading and has no cooldown.
# Authority
`pool_admin` OR `protocol_admin`, AND Treasury PDA.
# Used by
`protocol_admin::pool_set_swaps_enabled` (CPI).

instructions.name: set_token_active
docs: Set a token's `is_active` flag. When `false`, swaps whose INPUT token
is `token_index` revert (`TokenInactive`); the token can still be
bought (as output) and liquidity ops are unaffected.
# Authority
`pool.pool_admin` OR `config.protocol_admin` (Treasury PDA). The
Treasury path is reachable by admin OR supervisor via
`protocol_admin::pool_set_token_active`.

instructions.name: swap
docs: Swap one pool token for another using `calc_out_given_in`.
# Parameters
* `amount_in`         — raw input token units (pre-fee).
* `minimum_amount_out`— slippage floor.
* `token_in_index`    — index in `pool.token_mints`.
* `token_out_index`   — different index in `pool.token_mints`.
# Used by
User wallets, SDK `SwapClient`, single-token-liquidity helper.

accounts.name: user_token_account_in
docs: User's input-token account. Mint and owner cross-checked.

accounts.name: vault_in
docs: Pool input vault. ATA(pool, mint_in, token_program_in) — verified
in handler.

instructions.name: withdraw_sol
docs: Drain lamports from a coffer-pool-owned account, leaving at least
the rent-exempt minimum.
# Authority
Treasury PDA only.
# Parameters
* `amount` — lamports; must be > 0 and ≤
`source.lamports() - rent_exempt_minimum(source.data_len())`.
# Used by
`protocol_admin::pool_withdraw_sol` (CPI).

types.name: AssetConfig
docs: `CofferPool` v4 — per-pool state for a weighted AMM with virtual liquidity.
Storage layout: **Array-of-Structs (AoS)**. Per-token data lives in
`tokens: [TokenSlot; MAX_TOKENS]`. Each `TokenSlot` carries TWO nested
sub-structs:
- `config: AssetConfig`     — admin-controlled, rarely changes (mint,
token_program, weight, max_selloff, period).
- `dynamics: AssetDynamics` — auto-updated by user txs (balances,
protocol_fees_owed, sliding-window selloff state).
This mirrors Solend / MarginFi / Kamino's `Reserve { config, ... }`
pattern. Reading per-token data is a single struct lookup; auditors
see at a glance which fields a user can mutate vs which need pool
admin authority.
## Storage layout — DO NOT REORDER
Backends (`onchainPoolFetcher.ts`, indexer) read fields by raw offset.
Adding fields is OK if appended at the END (before the trailing
reserve of the CURRENT block) and that reserve shrinks accordingly.
Inserting in the middle would require rewriting existing accounts.
## v6.1 layout bump (L0): 1683 → 2304 bytes
Every pre-v6.1 field keeps its byte offset; the legacy `reserved: [u8;
16]` block (with its `V5M1` marker) is untouched. A v6.1 block is
APPENDED after it: `layout_version`, `token_decimals`, `reserved_v61`.
Existing 1683-byte pools are grown in place by the permissionless
`migrate_pool_layout_v61` instruction; until then every other
instruction fails with `LayoutVersionMismatch` (see
`AccountDeserialize` below — the account SIZE is the version marker).
### Carve-out order for `reserved_v61` (later v6.1 tasks)
New fields are inserted immediately BEFORE `reserved_v61`, in this
order, and `reserved_v61` shrinks by the same amount so `LEN` stays
2304 and every earlier offset is stable. Byte estimates:
| task | fields                                                       | bytes | offsets | status |
| T14  | `creator_fee_bps: u16` @1694, `creator_fees_owed: [u64; MAX_TOKENS]` @1696 |  82   | 1694..1776 | carved (first: T14 landed before T12) |
| T12  | `surge_fees_owed: [u64; MAX_TOKENS]` @1776 (LP-claimable NAV bucket) |  80   | 1776..1856 | carved |
| T7   | `deposit_fee_bps: u16` @1856, `withdraw_fee_bps: u16` @1858, `liquidity_fee_lock: u8` @1860 |   5   | 1856..1861 | carved |
| T6   | `range_manager_locked: bool`                                 |   1   | 1861 | carved |

| T3   | `pool_admin_delay_secs: u32` @1862, `pool_admin_epoch: u32` @1866, `pending_pool_admin_eta: i64` @1870, 10 typed pending slots (`eta: i64` + absolute payload) @1878..2054 — see `COOLDOWN_BLOCK_LEN` | 192 | 1862..2054 | carved |

| T9   | `hook_program: Pubkey` @2054, `hook_flags: u16` @2086, `hook_disabled: u8` @2088, `hook_fee_min: u32` @2089, `hook_fee_max: u32` @2093, `hook_max_cu: u32` @2097, `hook_accounts_len: u8` @2101 — see `HOOK_BLOCK_LEN` | 48 | 2054..2102 | carved (AFTER T3) |
| T2/T10 | `seeded: bool` + pad                                       |   2   | | |
| total carved (estimate)                                             | ≈ 410 | | 408 done (82 T14 + 80 T12 + 5 T7 + 1 T6 + 192 T3 + 48 T9, all real fields) |
| left in `reserved_v61` after all of the above                       | ≈ 200 (≥ 200 required) | | 202 now |
The T9 hook block (48 B) sits AFTER the T3 block @2054..2102 (the T9
branch carved it @1862 on a T3-less base and it was relocated at the
merge), leaving 202 B (T2/T10's 2 B ⇒ exactly the 200 B floor). Nothing
else may be carved without packing the T3 slots (e.g.
`PendingSetRangeManagerConfig` 24 → 22, `PendingSetTokenActive` eta as
T3 slot order inside the cooldown block (all `eta` fields are `i64`,
`0` = empty; the pool-admin transfer reuses `pending_pool_admin` for its
payload and only adds an `eta`):
| kind | field | payload | offset | size |
| — | `pool_admin_delay_secs: u32` | | 1862 | 4 |
| — | `pool_admin_epoch: u32` | | 1866 | 4 |
| 0 TransferPoolAdmin | `pending_pool_admin_eta` | (`pending_pool_admin` @98) | 1870 | 8 |
| 1 SetDelay | `pending_set_delay` | `secs: u32` | 1878 | 12 |
| 2 SetSwapFeeRate | `pending_set_swap_fee_rate` | `rate: u32` | 1890 | 12 |
| 3 SetCreatorFeeBps | `pending_set_creator_fee_bps` | `bps: u16` | 1902 | 10 |
| 4 SetLiquidityFees | `pending_set_liquidity_fees` | `deposit_fee_bps: u16, withdraw_fee_bps: u16` | 1912 | 12 |
| 5 LockLiquidityFees | `pending_lock_liquidity_fees` | — | 1924 | 8 |
| 6 LockRangeManager | `pending_lock_range_manager` | — | 1932 | 8 |
| 7 SetRangeManager | `pending_set_range_manager` | `manager: Pubkey, enabled: bool` | 1940 | 41 |
| 8 SetRangeManagerConfig | `pending_set_range_manager_config` | `u16, u16, u32, u32, u32` | 1981 | 24 |
| 9 SetMaxSelloff | `pending_set_max_selloff` | `params_hash: [u8; 32]` | 2005 | 40 |
| 10 SetTokenActive | `pending_set_token_active` | `token_index: u8` (always `true`) | 2045 | 9 |
| | T9 hook block (`HOOK_BLOCK_LEN`) | | 2054 | 48 |
The absolute offsets above are the contract between branches: the T12
block (80 B @1776) was held by a same-sized placeholder on the T7 / T6
branches so the T7 fields sit at 1856..1861 and `range_manager_locked`
at 1861; the T12 merge replaced the placeholder with `surge_fees_owed`
at the same offset. The T3 cooldown block sits at 1862..2054 directly
after the T6 flag and the T9 hook block follows it at 2054..2102 (the T9
branch had carved @1862 on a T3-less base; the merge moved the block
behind T3 as the carve table always said). Offsets of landed fields
never moved.
### Vault bookkeeping (v6.1, T14 + T12)
For every slot `i`: `vault_i.amount == actual_balance_i +
protocol_fees_owed_i + creator_fees_owed_i + surge_fees_owed_i`
(`vault_bookkeeping_total`). A vault may hold MORE (a direct transfer
credits nobody), never less while the pool is not bricked. Only
`actual_balance` prices trades; the two owed buckets are claimable by
the protocol admin (`collect_protocol_fees`) and the pool admin
(`claim_creator_fees`) respectively and never by each other. The T12
surge bucket belongs to the LP holders collectively: it is outside the
curve (never traded, never priced) but it IS LP capital — a deposit
buys into it pro rata and a burn pays it out pro rata, so the LP token's
net asset value per unit is `(actual + surge_fees_owed) / supply`
(`nav_balances`). The T7 deposit / withdraw fees never create a bucket:
the withheld LP (deposit) and the withheld tokens (withdraw) stay in the
reserves, i.e. in `actual_balance`.
## Derived (not stored) state
- `lp_mint`        — derived as `[LP_MINT_SEED, pool]` PDA.
- `lp_total_supply`— read from `lp_mint.supply` at runtime.
- `token_vaults[i]` — derived as ATA(pool, mint, tokens[i].config.token_program).
- `token_decimals`  — pinned on the pool since v6.1 (FIX-6); the live
mint must still agree with it on every transfer.

fields.name: mint
docs: Token mint pubkey for this slot. `Pubkey::default()` past `token_count`.

fields.name: token_program
docs: SPL Token or Token-2022 program ID for this token's vault/transfers.

fields.name: normalized_weight
docs: Normalised weight in basis points (sum across active slots == 10_000).

fields.name: max_selloff_pct
docs: Max cumulative sell volume of this token per sliding window,
expressed as a **percentage of the token's `virtual_balance`**
captured at window start, in units of `PERCENT_SCALE` (10_000 =
100%, so 1000 = 10%; resolution 0.01%). `0` disables the check for
this token. Must be `<= PERCENT_SCALE`. Set by pool_admin only.
The absolute cap for a window is `floor(max_selloff_pct *
vb_snapshot / PERCENT_SCALE)`, where `vb_snapshot` is
`AssetDynamics::selloff_vb_snapshot` (taken at window open). Using a
per-window snapshot — not the live `virtual_balance` — prevents an
in-window base-inflation bypass (see `math::max_selloff`).

fields.name: max_selloff_period_length
docs: Length of the sliding window in seconds. Ignored when
`max_selloff_pct == 0`. Set by pool_admin only.

fields.name: variable_fee_threshold_pct
docs: Variable sell-off **surge fee** curve (per token, `PERCENT_SCALE`
units; 10_000 = 100%). The fee rises as the token's max-selloff
window fills and is charged on `amount_out`, routed 100% to the
protocol bucket (`protocol_fees_owed`), never to LPs. See
`math::surge_fee`. The fee is active only when `max_selloff_pct > 0`
(it reads the window fill ratio) AND `fee_slope_high_pct > 0`.
Window fill ratio at which the surge fee starts (below it the fee is
0). E.g. 8000 = surge begins at 80% window fill.

fields.name: variable_fee_slope_low_pct
docs: Surge fee at the threshold (lower point of the curve).

fields.name: variable_fee_slope_high_pct
docs: Surge fee at ~100% window fill (upper point of the curve). Must be
`>= fee_slope_low_pct` and `<= PERCENT_SCALE`.

fields.name: is_active
docs: Per-token kill switch for the **input** side of swaps. When `false`,
swaps whose INPUT token is this one revert (`TokenInactive`); the
token can still be bought (as swap output) and liquidity ops are
unaffected. Defaults to `true` (active). Flipped by `set_token_active`
(pool-admin or protocol-admin/supervisor). Used to stop accepting a
compromised token without pausing the whole pool.

fields.name: variable_fee_slope_mid_pct
docs: Surge fee at the KINK — the middle of the three points that define the
curve. Between `variable_fee_threshold_pct` and this point the fee runs
linearly from `variable_fee_slope_low_pct` to here; beyond it, linearly
from here to `variable_fee_slope_high_pct` at full window fill.
This is the "target utilisation" shape lending protocols use (Evaa,
Aave, Compound): gentle while the window fills normally, steep once it
is nearly exhausted. Must satisfy
`slope_low <= slope_mid <= slope_high` — a fee that fell as the window
filled would invert the brake.

fields.name: variable_fee_kink_pct
docs: Window fill at which the curve kinks, in WHOLE PERCENT (0..=100), not
`PERCENT_SCALE` units — one byte is all that was left, and 1% is ample
resolution for a breakpoint.
`0` means "no kink": the curve degenerates to a single straight line
from `slope_low` at the threshold to `slope_high` at full fill, which
is what every pool written by the previous layout decodes as.
Must sit strictly between the threshold and full fill when set.

fields.name: virtual_balance
docs: Virtual balance (raw token units) used by the coffer invariant
math. Decoupled from `actual_balance` to enable concentrated
liquidity. Updated by swap / add_liquidity / remove_liquidity.

fields.name: actual_balance
docs: The LP-owned portion of this token's vault, in raw units.
It does NOT equal the vault's `amount`. The invariant is
`vault.amount == actual_balance + protocol_fees_owed +
creator_fees_owed[i] + surge_fees_owed[i]`
(`CofferPool::vault_bookkeeping_total`): the protocol's and the pool
admin's fee buckets sit in the same vault but are not LP capital, and
`collect_protocol_fees` / `claim_creator_fees` pay them out without
touching `actual_balance`; the surge bucket (v6.1 T12) is LP capital
that is kept OUT of the curve and paid pro rata on `remove_liquidity`.
Sizing a withdrawal or a deposit ratio against the raw vault balance
would therefore hand LPs the uncollected fees.
Reads of the vault should either use this field or subtract every
owed bucket explicitly; they are only equal on a pool whose fees
have just been collected and whose surge bucket is empty.

fields.name: protocol_fees_owed
docs: Accumulated protocol fees for this token (raw units), awaiting
`collect_protocol_fees`. Stored separately from `actual_balance`
so LP value isn't diluted by uncollected fees.

fields.name: previous_selloff
docs: Sliding-window rate limiter: amount sold in the PREVIOUS window
(Cloudflare-style approximation, Solend RateLimiter pattern).

fields.name: current_selloff
docs: Amount sold in the CURRENT window.

fields.name: window_start_timestamp
docs: `Clock::unix_timestamp` when the current window started. Set to
`now()` at pool init.

fields.name: selloff_vb_snapshot
docs: Snapshot of this token's `virtual_balance` taken when the current
max-selloff window opened. The window's absolute cap is
`floor(config.max_selloff_pct * selloff_vb_snapshot / PERCENT_SCALE)`.
Snapshotting (rather than reading live `virtual_balance`) keeps the
cap un-inflatable within a window — selling raises the live vb, but
not this snapshot. `0` ⇒ uninitialised (re-captured on next check).

types.name: CofferPool
docs: The account traits are implemented by hand (instead of `#[account]`) so
that `AccountDeserialize::try_deserialize` can refuse a pool whose
`data_len != LEN` with the explicit `LayoutVersionMismatch` error. The
expansion mirrors `anchor_attribute_account` 0.32.1 exactly apart from
that one length check; `Discriminator`, `Owner`, `AccountSerialize` and
the Borsh derives are unchanged.

fields.name: config
docs: `CofferPoolConfig` this pool inherits governance from. Pinned at
init, used both as a PDA seed and at runtime in admin-instruction
constraints (`pool.config == config.key()`).

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump seed for the pool PDA. Stored so signer-seed reconstruction is
O(1) instead of an expensive `find_program_address` per CPI.

fields.name: token_count
docs: Number of active tokens in the pool, in [MIN_TOKENS, MAX_TOKENS] =
[2, 10]. Slots beyond `token_count` are zeroed and ignored.

fields.name: pool_id
docs: User-chosen 64-bit salt baked into the PDA seeds, allowing multiple
pools per config without re-deploying. Unique per (config, pool_id).

fields.name: swap_fee_rate
docs: Swap fee in hundredths of a basis point (precision
`SWAP_FEE_PRECISION` = 1_000_000). 100_000 = 10% (current cap).

fields.name: protocol_fee_rate
docs: Share of each swap fee taken by the protocol, in basis points
(precision `PROTOCOL_FEE_PRECISION` = 10_000). 5_000 = 50% (cap).

fields.name: created_at
docs: Pool creation `Clock::unix_timestamp`. Informational only.

fields.name: pool_enabled
docs: Master kill switch — when `false`, swaps and add/remove liquidity
all revert. Only `protocol_admin` can flip this.

fields.name: swaps_enabled
docs: Trading switch — `false` blocks swaps but still allows LP
add/remove. Either `pool_admin` or `config.protocol_admin` can flip.

fields.name: pool_admin
docs: Per-pool admin. Owns: rotate swap_fee_rate, toggle swaps_enabled,
set range_manager, set max_selloff, transfer/disable itself.

fields.name: pending_pool_admin
docs: Pending successor for `pool_admin` during a 2-step transfer.

fields.name: range_manager
docs: Pubkey allowed to call `range_manager_update`. `Pubkey::default()`
⇒ no manager set.

fields.name: range_manager_enabled
docs: `false` ⇒ all `range_manager_update` calls revert.

fields.name: range_manager_max_vb_change_pct
docs: Max per-update change to a token's `virtual_balance`, as a
percentage of its current value, in `PERCENT_SCALE` units
(10_000 = 100%; 500 = 5%). Enforced per token in
`range_manager_update`.

fields.name: range_manager_max_weight_change_pct
docs: Max per-update change to a token's `normalized_weight`, same
`PERCENT_SCALE` units.

fields.name: tokens
docs: All per-token state. Slot `i` is for the i-th token. Slots past
`token_count` are zero-initialised and ignored.

fields.name: lookup_table
docs: Per-pool Address Lookup Table address. Holds pool-scoped accounts
(pool PDA, LP mint, vaults, mints, token programs) so client SDKs
can build VersionedTransactions for `add_liquidity` / `remove_liquidity`
without hitting the 1232-byte legacy-tx ceiling on multi-token pools.
`Pubkey::default()` ⇒ ALT not yet initialised. SDK falls back to
legacy tx (will only work for small pools). Set by `initialize_pool_alt`,
frozen on-chain so depositors don't worry about authority abuse.

fields.name: _deprecated_banned_extensions
docs: Bytes 1651..1659 of the account. Until v6.1 this held the per-pool
`banned_extensions` Token-2022 policy bitmap snapshot. The policy was
removed in v6.1 (T19): the pool creator alone decides which mints go
into a pool and the frontend discloses the extensions they carry.
Mint admission is now purely structural
(`util::token::validate_mint_for_admission`).
Not trailing (it sits between `lookup_table` and
`range_manager_max_leverage_bps`), so it cannot be folded into
`reserved`. Existing pools still carry their old bitmap here; fresh
pools write `0`. No code path reads it. `migrate_to_v5` keeps its
`== 0` precondition on these bytes as part of the "untouched legacy
layout" proof (I-11). A later task may reuse these 8 bytes only
after an explicit migration instruction zeroes them — existing pools
hold non-zero values that would otherwise be misread.

fields.name: range_manager_max_leverage_bps
docs: Absolute ceiling on `virtual_balance / actual_balance` that the range
manager may leave a token at, in basis points (10_000 = 1.0×). `0`
disables the band.
The per-update percentage caps velocity, not distance: measured
against the live value each call, 5% steps compound to ~2.65× in 20
updates and ~131× in 100, so a manager — or a malfunctioning bot —
can walk the pool price arbitrarily far using only individually legal
moves. This band is the distance limit.
Anchored to `actual_balance` rather than to a captured snapshot on
purpose: real reserves only move when capital actually enters or
leaves, so the baseline cannot go stale the way a stored snapshot
does. Tokens with `actual_balance == 0` (sidelined) are exempt —
there is no real capital to anchor against.
Appended at the END (before `reserved`) per the layout rule above, so
every pre-existing field keeps its byte offset. Pre-upgrade pools
decode this as `0` (band disabled), which is the back-compatible
reading.

fields.name: range_manager_min_leverage_bps
docs: Lower half of the range manager's absolute envelope: the SMALLEST
`virtual_balance / actual_balance` ratio it may leave a token at, in
`PERCENT_SCALE` units. `0` disables the floor.
The ceiling alone was not an envelope. Output is priced off VIRTUAL
balances, so DEPRESSING a token's virtual balance makes the pool
believe it holds less than it does, and a sale into that token moves
the price far more than it should — the seller takes the other side's
real reserves at a fabricated rate. Fifty individually-legal 5% steps
took a 1M/1M pool's virtual balance down to ~77k in testing, after
which selling 100k returned ~565k instead of ~91k. Every step passed
the ceiling, because the ceiling only ever looks upward.
Checked on the same terms as the ceiling: only over the slots a call
actually writes, and skipped for sidelined tokens (`actual_balance ==
0`), which have no capital to anchor a ratio against.

fields.name: reserved
docs: LEGACY padding block (bytes 1667..1683 of the account). Shrank 24 → 20
when `range_manager_max_leverage_bps` was carved out of it, then
20 → 16 for `range_manager_min_leverage_bps`. Since v6.1 it is FROZEN:
`reserved[..4]` holds the one-shot `V5M1` migration marker and the
remaining 12 bytes are part of the `migrate_to_v5` "untouched legacy
layout" proof (I-11). Nothing new is ever carved from here; new
fields come out of `reserved_v61` below.

fields.name: layout_version
docs: Version of the appended block. `1` = v6.1 (`LAYOUT_VERSION_V61`).
Never `0` on a decodable account: a pool that has not been through
`migrate_pool_layout_v61` is still 1683 bytes and fails
`AccountDeserialize` with `LayoutVersionMismatch` before any handler
runs, so the account SIZE is the real marker and this byte is a sanity
pin for off-chain decoders and future bumps.

fields.name: token_decimals
docs: Per-slot mint decimals (audit FIX-6), pinned at `initialize_pool` and
filled by `migrate_pool_layout_v61` from the live mint accounts (the
only on-chain source: token accounts do not carry decimals). Every
transfer-profile build asserts the live mint still reports the pinned
value, so a mint closed (`MintCloseAuthority`) and re-created at the
same address with different decimals is refused instead of mis-scaled.
Slots past `token_count` are 0.

fields.name: creator_fee_bps
docs: Pool admin's ("creator's") share of the LP remainder of every swap
fee and surge fee, in basis points of `CREATOR_FEE_PRECISION`
(`0..=MAX_CREATOR_FEE_BPS`, i.e. up to 100% of what is left after the
protocol's cut). `0` = off. Set at `initialize_pool` (default 0) and
by the pool admin via `set_creator_fee_bps`; cleared to 0 by
`disable_pool_admin`. Layout-migrated pre-v6.1 pools decode `0`.
Never changes the trader's price: it only re-splits the fee.

fields.name: creator_fees_owed
docs: Per-slot accrual of the creator share (raw units, slot order), owed
to the CURRENT `pool_admin` and swept by `claim_creator_fees`. Part
of the vault bookkeeping (`vault_bookkeeping_total`), never part of
`actual_balance`, so it is excluded from pricing and LP payouts.
Slots past `token_count` stay 0.

fields.name: surge_fees_owed
docs: v6.1 (T12): the LP holders' share of every MaxSellOff surge fee, per
slot (raw units, slot order; 80 B @1776). On `swap` the surge charged
on the OUTPUT token goes through the same cascade as the base fee
(`math::split_fee`: protocol ceil → creator floor → LP remainder) and
the LP remainder lands HERE instead of in the reserves. The bucket is
part of the vault bookkeeping (`vault_bookkeeping_total`) and of the
LP token's NAV (`nav_balances`), but NOT of `actual_balance`: it is
never traded (swaps are bounded by `actual_balance`), never priced
and never moved by the range manager.
Entitlement is pro rata by LP supply AT BURN and travels with the LP
token: `remove_liquidity` pays `floor(surge_fees_owed_i · burn /
supply)` next to the reserve share (one transfer per token), and
`add_liquidity` buys in (`floor(surge_fees_owed_i · ratio)` of the
NAV-based credit is booked here) so a deposit-then-burn in the same
slot extracts nothing (JIT-neutral). No standalone claim instruction;
a partial burn is the claim. Zero on every migrated pool
(`migrate_pool_layout_v61` zeroes the tail) and at birth. Slots past
`token_count` stay 0.

fields.name: deposit_fee_bps
docs: v6.1 (T7): deposit fee as a haircut on the LP minted by
`add_liquidity`, in `LIQUIDITY_FEE_PRECISION` units (10_000 = 100%).
`lp_minted = lp_gross − ceil(lp_gross · bps / 10_000)`; the full
basket is still credited to the reserves, so the withheld LP's share
of it accrues to the existing LP holders. 100% closes deposits
(`DepositFeeConsumesAll`). `seed_liquidity`, `fund_sidelined_token`
and the STLD zap's own swaps are exempt (the zap's final join is an
`add_liquidity` CPI and pays it). Byte 1856. Pool-admin setter
`set_liquidity_fees`, frozen for ever by `lock_liquidity_fees`.

fields.name: withdraw_fee_bps
docs: v6.1 (T7): withdraw fee as a haircut on every token payout of
`remove_liquidity`, same units: `payout_i = gross_i − ceil(gross_i ·
bps / 10_000)`. The withheld tokens stay in `actual_balance`
(remaining LPs' reserves; never a protocol or creator bucket). 100%
closes withdrawals (`WithdrawFeeConsumesAll`). Bytes 1858..1860.

fields.name: liquidity_fee_lock
docs: v6.1 (T7): bit `LIQUIDITY_FEE_LOCK_FROZEN` (0x01) ⇒ `set_liquidity_fees`
is rejected for ever (lowering included). Set once by
`lock_liquidity_fees`, never cleared by any instruction; survives
admin transfers and `disable_pool_admin`. Other bits reserved (0).
Byte 1860.

fields.name: range_manager_locked
docs: v6.1 (T6): one-way "no range manager, ever" flag (@1861). Set only
by `lock_range_manager` (pool admin; requires `range_manager ==
Pubkey::default()` and `!range_manager_enabled`); no instruction
clears it. While set, `set_range_manager` (every caller, including
the protocol-admin disable path), `set_range_manager_config` and
`range_manager_update` fail with `RangeManagerLocked`. `false` on
every migrated pool (zeroed tail) and on every fresh pool.

fields.name: pool_admin_delay_secs
docs: Seconds every D-class pool-admin action must wait between proposal
and execution. `0` (fresh and migrated pools) ⇒ the direct
instructions work as before; `> 0` ⇒ they fail with
`CooldownRequired` and only `propose_pool_action` → `execute_*`
applies. Changed by `set_pool_admin_delay` (direct at 0) or through
the queue (waits `max(old, new)`); `0..=MAX_DELAY_SECS`. @1862.

fields.name: pool_admin_epoch
docs: Incremented on every pool-admin change (`accept_pool_admin_transfer`,
`disable_pool_admin`); every pending slot is cleared at the same
time, so a proposal never survives the key that made it. @1866.

fields.name: pending_pool_admin_eta
docs: `eta` of the in-flight pool-admin transfer (`pending_pool_admin`
@98 holds the successor): `accept_pool_admin_transfer` requires
`eta <= now <= eta + GRACE`. `0` when no transfer is pending. @1870.

fields.name: hook_program
docs: Hook program the pool CPIs before / after swaps and liquidity
operations (`Pubkey::default()` = no hook; every migrated pool). Set
once by `initialize_pool(.., hook_config)`; immutable — there is no
setter, so nothing for the admin cooldown to gate. @2054.

fields.name: hook_flags
docs: `coffer_hook_interface::flags` bitmap: which callbacks run, whether
`before-swap` may override the swap fee (`DYNAMIC_FEE`) and whether a
disabled hook pauses swaps / adds (`PAUSE_WHEN_DISABLED`). Bits 8..15
are 0. Immutable. @2086.

fields.name: hook_disabled
docs: Protocol-admin emergency switch (`set_hook_disabled`, instant, no
cooldown): `1` ⇒ no callback is invoked; swaps / adds proceed with the
base fee, or fail with `HookPaused` when `PAUSE_WHEN_DISABLED` is set.
Removes always proceed. While disabled the hook account slice is NOT
part of the remaining-accounts tail. @2088.

fields.name: hook_fee_min
docs: Lower bound of a `before-swap` fee override (hundredths of bps,
`SWAP_FEE_PRECISION`); an override below it is clamped up. Floor 0
(`HOOK_FEE_FLOOR`, revisit with H-09). Immutable. @2089.

fields.name: hook_fee_max
docs: Upper bound of a fee override (≤ `MAX_SWAP_FEE_RATE`); an override
above it is clamped down. Immutable. @2093.

fields.name: hook_max_cu
docs: Compute-unit ceiling per callback, measured around the CPI (incl. the
invoke base cost); above it the operation fails with `HookCuExceeded`.
`HOOK_MIN_CU..=HOOK_MAX_CU_CAP`. Immutable. @2097.

fields.name: hook_accounts_len
docs: Number of accounts in the hook slice (`[hook_program, hook_caller,
extras..]`) that every hooked instruction's remaining-accounts tail
begins with while the hook is active. `HOOK_MIN_ACCOUNTS..=
HOOK_MAX_ACCOUNTS`. Immutable. @2101.

fields.name: reserved_v61
docs: v6.1 reserve. See the struct doc for the carve-out order and the byte
budget. Zero on every v6.1 account (fresh or migrated); later tasks
insert their fields directly before it and shrink it, keeping `LEN`

fields.name: protocol_admin
docs: Protocol-level admin. Allowed to: pause pools, change
`protocol_fee_rate`, collect protocol fees, drain via
`debug_withdraw_liquidity`, withdraw SOL from program-owned
accounts, and rotate itself via the
pending/accept flow. Set to a designated authority (typically the
Treasury PDA of the `protocol-admin` program) at config init.

fields.name: pending_protocol_admin
docs: Pending successor for `protocol_admin` during a 2-step transfer.
`Pubkey::default()` ⇒ no transfer in flight.

fields.name: default_protocol_fee_rate
docs: Stored by `initialize_config` (basis points, ≤ `MAX_PROTOCOL_FEE_RATE`).
Until v6.1 it was copied onto every new pool; since T15 the pool
field is the only source of truth — `initialize_pool` writes the
program constant `DEFAULT_PROTOCOL_FEE_RATE` and **no code path reads
this field**. Kept in the layout (ABI, `ConfigInitialized` event) and
informational for off-chain readers only.

fields.name: _deprecated_extension_policy
docs: Bytes 74..90 of the account (no discriminator offset: 66..82 of the
payload). Until v6.1 these held the `banned_extensions` /
`hard_banned_extensions` Token-2022 extension-policy bitmaps. The
policy was removed in v6.1 (T19): the pool admin alone decides which
mints go into a pool and the frontend discloses the extensions they
carry. Mint admission is now purely structural
(`util::token::validate_mint_for_admission`).
Existing configs still carry non-zero bytes here. No code path reads
them; they are not part of the zero-check that `reserved` is subject
to. A later task may reuse these 16 bytes only after an explicit
migration instruction zeroes them.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Forward-compatibility padding so future fields can be added without
migrating existing config accounts. Shrank 120 → 112 when the
(now deprecated) second policy bitmap was carved out of the tail.

types.name: ConfigInitializedV2
docs: `initialize_config` (actor: the Treasury PDA via
`protocol_admin::pool_initialize_config`; `payer` funded the rent).
Creation event: every field is the account's initial value.
Re-cut of `ConfigInitialized` (dropped the always-zero T19
`banned_extensions`).

fields.name: default_protocol_fee_rate
docs: Stored on the config; informational since v6.1 (T15).

types.name: CreatorFeeBpsUpdated
docs: `set_creator_fee_bps` / `execute_set_creator_fee_bps` (actor:
`pool_admin`, T14).

types.name: CreatorFeesClaimedV2
docs: `claim_creator_fees` (actor: `pool_admin`, T14). Before:
`creator_fees_owed[i] = token_amounts[i]`; after: 0. `recipients[i]`
as in `ProtocolFeesCollectedV2`. Re-cut of `CreatorFeesClaimed`.

types.name: DebugLiquidityWithdrawnV2
docs: `debug_withdraw_liquidity` (actor: `protocol_admin`). The pool's
bookkeeping is deliberately NOT updated (the pool is bricked); the vault
balances before / after make the gap visible on the wire. Slots with
`token_amounts[i] == 0` are not touched: their recipient is
`Pubkey::default()` and both vault balances are reported as 0 (the vault
account is not read). Re-cut of `DebugLiquidityWithdrawn`.

types.name: HookConfig
docs: `initialize_pool(.., hook_config: Option<HookConfig>)` — the immutable
per-pool hook configuration. Stored field-for-field on the pool
(`CofferPool::hook_*`).

fields.name: program
docs: Executable program the pool will CPI. Not this program, not a token /
system / lookup-table / protocol-admin program.

fields.name: flags
docs: `coffer_hook_interface::flags` bitmap; at least one callback bit,
no reserved bits, `DYNAMIC_FEE ⇒ BEFORE_SWAP`.

fields.name: fee_min
docs: Fee-override clamp (hundredths of bps). `HOOK_FEE_FLOOR ≤ fee_min ≤
fee_max ≤ MAX_SWAP_FEE_RATE`; both 0 unless `DYNAMIC_FEE`.

fields.name: max_cu
docs: Per-callback CU ceiling, `HOOK_MIN_CU..=HOOK_MAX_CU_CAP`.

fields.name: accounts_len
docs: Hook slice length, `HOOK_MIN_ACCOUNTS..=HOOK_MAX_ACCOUNTS`.

types.name: HookDisabledSet
docs: `set_hook_disabled` (actor: `protocol_admin`, T9).

fields.name: authority
docs: The Treasury PDA (`config.protocol_admin`).

fields.name: pause_when_disabled
docs: `hook_flags & PAUSE_WHEN_DISABLED != 0`.

types.name: HookInvoked
docs: Secondary event: one per hook callback actually CPI'd (never for a
skipped one).
* `callback` — `coffer_hook_interface::Callback` as `u8` (0 on-register,
1 before-swap, 2 after-swap, 3/4 add, 5/6 remove)
* `verdict`  — 0 Allow, 1 Deny (informational on the remove callbacks)
* `has_fee_override` / `fee_override` — as RETURNED by the hook (before
clamping); `SwapV2.effective_fee_rate` is the applied rate
* `cu_used`  — compute units measured around the CPI

types.name: LiquidityAddedV2
docs: `add_liquidity` and `seed_liquidity` (`is_seed`; actor: any user /
`pool_admin` for the seed). Carries the basket actually taken and the
before / after of every field the join mutates: `actual_balance`,
`virtual_balance`, `surge_fees_owed` (T12 buy-in) on every slot and the
LP supply. `protocol_fees_owed` / `creator_fees_owed` are untouched by a
join and therefore not repeated.
Re-cut of `LiquidityAdded` (+ before / after vectors; −
`initial_lp_supply` = `lp_amount` when `is_seed`).
Invariants: `credited_amounts[i] = token_amounts[i] − transfer fee`;
`actual_after[i] = actual_before[i] + credited_amounts[i] −
surge_buy_in[i]`; `surge_after[i] = surge_before[i] + surge_buy_in[i]`;
`lp_supply_after = lp_supply_before + lp_amount`; `lp_amount =
lp_gross − deposit_fee_lp` (T7; the seed is fee-exempt:
`deposit_fee_lp = 0`).

fields.name: token_amounts
docs: Charged to the user (gross), per slot — may be below the ceiling the
caller passed.

fields.name: credited_amounts
docs: Booked by the pool (net of transfer fees).

fields.name: surge_buy_in
docs: Part of each credit that bought into the LP surge bucket (T12).

fields.name: lp_amount
docs: LP minted to the user (net of the deposit fee).

fields.name: deposit_fee_lp
docs: LP withheld by the deposit fee (T7).

fields.name: deposit_fee_bps
docs: `pool.deposit_fee_bps` in force.

types.name: LiquidityFeesLocked
docs: `lock_liquidity_fees` / `execute_lock_liquidity_fees` (actor:
`pool_admin`, T7): `liquidity_fee_lock` 0 → 1, the rates carried are
frozen for ever.

types.name: LiquidityFeesUpdated
docs: `set_liquidity_fees` / `execute_set_liquidity_fees` (actor:
`pool_admin`, T7).

types.name: LiquidityRemovedV2
docs: `remove_liquidity` / `remove_liquidity_bypass_hooks` (`hooks_bypassed`;
actor: any LP). Before / after of every field the burn mutates.
Re-cut of `LiquidityRemoved` (+ `requested_lp`, `transfer_fees_out`,
`hooks_bypassed`, before / after vectors).
Invariants: `lp_amount ≤ requested_lp` (capped at `supply −
MIN_LP_SUPPLY`); the user's transfer per slot is `token_amounts[i] +
surge_amounts[i]`, credited `− transfer_fees_out[i]`;
`withdraw_fee_amounts[i]` was withheld across both parts (T7);
`actual_after[i] = actual_before[i] − token_amounts[i]`;
`surge_after[i] = surge_before[i] − surge_amounts[i]`;
`lp_supply_after = lp_supply_before − lp_amount`.

fields.name: requested_lp
docs: The caller's `lp_amount` parameter.

fields.name: lp_amount
docs: Effective burn.

fields.name: token_amounts
docs: Net reserve payout per slot.

fields.name: surge_amounts
docs: Net surge-bucket payout per slot (T12).

fields.name: withdraw_fee_amounts
docs: Withdraw fee withheld per slot (T7).

fields.name: withdraw_fee_bps
docs: `pool.withdraw_fee_bps` in force.

fields.name: transfer_fees_out
docs: Token-2022 transfer fee per slot on the user's credit.

fields.name: hooks_bypassed
docs: `true` for `remove_liquidity_bypass_hooks` (T9).

types.name: LpMetadataArgs
docs: Metadata of a pool's LP token, set once at `initialize_pool`.
Borsh wire size: `4 + name.len() + 4 + symbol.len() + 4 + uri.len()`
(15 bytes minimum, 254 bytes at the limits).

fields.name: name
docs: Display name, 1..=32 bytes of printable UTF-8 (no control characters,
no leading/trailing whitespace). Unicode is allowed.

fields.name: symbol
docs: Ticker, 1..=10 bytes of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`.

fields.name: uri
docs: Off-chain JSON (Metaplex fungible standard), 1..=200 bytes, scheme
`https://`, `ipfs://` or `ar://`, no whitespace, no control chars.

types.name: MaxSelloffSetV2
docs: `set_max_selloff` / `execute_set_max_selloff` (actor: `pool_admin`).
`old_params[i]` / `new_params[i]` are the per-slot policy
(`SelloffParams`: cap pct, period, threshold, slope low / high, slope
mid, kink) before / after; `new_params` is the parameter vector as
passed. Re-cut of `MaxSelloffSet` (which lacked the mid / kink points).

types.name: PendingLock
docs: Payload-less slot (`LockLiquidityFees` kind 5, `LockRangeManager` kind 6).

types.name: PendingSetCreatorFeeBps
docs: Slot for `SetCreatorFeeBps` (kind 3).

types.name: PendingSetDelay
docs: Slot for `SetDelay` (kind 1): the new `pool_admin_delay_secs`.

types.name: PendingSetLiquidityFees
docs: Slot for `SetLiquidityFees` (kind 4).

types.name: PendingSetMaxSelloff
docs: Slot for `SetMaxSelloff` (kind 9). Up to 10 × 15-byte `SelloffParams`
do not fit inline, so the slot pins `sha256(borsh(params))`; the full
vector travels in `PoolActionProposed.payload` and must be resent to
`execute_set_max_selloff`, which re-hashes and re-validates it.

types.name: PendingSetRangeManager
docs: Slot for `SetRangeManager` (kind 7). Only the pool-admin path is queued;
the exact disable `(current, false)` is an emergency action and stays
direct.

types.name: PendingSetRangeManagerConfig
docs: Slot for `SetRangeManagerConfig` (kind 8), same five arguments.

types.name: PendingSetSwapFeeRate
docs: Slot for `SetSwapFeeRate` (kind 2).

types.name: PendingSetTokenActive
docs: Slot for the pool admin's `SetTokenActive(index, true)` (kind 10).
Re-enabling is the relaxing direction and therefore delayed; disabling
is an emergency action and stays direct.

types.name: PoolAction
docs: Proposal payload: the ABSOLUTE arguments the direct instruction takes.
`PoolActionProposed.payload` is `borsh(PoolAction)` (1-byte variant tag
first), so an indexer decodes it with the IDL type.

types.name: PoolActionCancelled
docs: `cancel_pool_action` (actor: `pool_admin`): slot `kind` cleared (kind 0
additionally emits `PoolAdminTransferCancelled`).

types.name: PoolActionExecuted
docs: Secondary event of every `execute_*` (next to the typed event of the
applied change): slot `kind` was cleared.

fields.name: eta
docs: The slot's `eta` (≤ `timestamp`).

types.name: PoolActionProposed
docs: `propose_pool_action` (actor: `pool_admin`): slot `kind` now holds
`payload` (`borsh(PoolAction)`, variant tag first) and becomes executable
at `eta`. A re-proposal of the same kind overwrites the previous one.

fields.name: kind
docs: `PoolActionKind` as `u8` (1 = SetDelay … 10 = SetTokenActive).

fields.name: epoch
docs: `pool_admin_epoch` at proposal time.

types.name: PoolAdminDelayChanged
docs: `set_pool_admin_delay` / `execute_set_delay` (actor: `pool_admin`):
`pool_admin_delay_secs` old → new; live slots are pushed to
`max(eta, now + new)` when the delay rises.

types.name: SelloffParams
docs: Per-token sell-off policy. One entry per active token (in pool order).
All `_pct` fields are in `PERCENT_SCALE` units (10_000 = 100%).

fields.name: max_selloff_pct
docs: Max cumulative sell volume per window, as a percent of the token's
virtual balance (snapshot at window open). `0` disables the cap
AND the surge fee for this token. Must be `<= PERCENT_SCALE`.

fields.name: period_length
docs: Sliding-window length in seconds. Must be `> 0` when
`max_selloff_pct > 0`.

fields.name: fee_threshold_pct
docs: Surge fee: window-fill ratio at which the fee starts (below it the
fee is 0). Must be `< PERCENT_SCALE` when `fee_slope_high_pct > 0`.

fields.name: fee_slope_low_pct
docs: Surge fee at the threshold (lower curve point).

fields.name: fee_slope_high_pct
docs: Surge fee at ~100% window fill (upper curve point). `0` disables the
surge fee. Must be `>= fee_slope_mid_pct` and `<= PERCENT_SCALE`.

fields.name: fee_slope_mid_pct
docs: Surge fee at the KINK — the middle of the three points.
Appended at the END of this struct, not slotted next to the other two
slope fields: Borsh encodes instruction arguments positionally, so
inserting mid-struct would silently reinterpret every later field for
clients built against the previous IDL.
Must satisfy `fee_slope_low_pct <= fee_slope_mid_pct <=
fee_slope_high_pct`.

fields.name: fee_kink_pct
docs: Window fill at which the curve kinks, in WHOLE PERCENT (0..=100).
`0` means "no kink": one straight line from `fee_slope_low_pct` at the
threshold to `fee_slope_high_pct` at full fill. When non-zero it must
sit STRICTLY between the threshold and full fill — a kink at either
end degenerates one of the two segments to zero width.

types.name: SelloffWindow
docs: The sliding sell-off window of `SwapV2.token_in_index` as it was advanced
by the swap (`math::max_selloff::check_and_advance`). Present only when
the input token has a cap (`max_selloff_pct > 0`). Window fill =
`effective_selloff / max_selloff_cap`; `cap = pct · vb_snapshot /
PERCENT_SCALE` (the policy itself is logged by `MaxSelloffSetV2`).

fields.name: effective_selloff_before
docs: Window fill BEFORE this swap's net input was added (the surge fee
integrates from here to `effective_selloff`).

fields.name: effective_selloff
docs: Window fill AFTER (`before + amount_in_net`), the value compared to
the cap.

types.name: SwapV2
docs: `swap` (actor: any user). Self-contained: parameters, the full fee
cascade, and the before / after of BOTH touched slots (no separate state
log). The indexer applies `in_after` / `out_after` to its pool row and
can verify `after == f(before, params)` per leg; `before` of a leg equals
`after` of the previous instruction on the same pool in log order.
Re-cut of `Swap` (+ indices, net / gross amounts, slot before / after,
window; − mints, `surge_fee_lp_amount` = `surge_fee_amount −
surge_protocol_fee_amount − surge_creator_fee_amount`).
Invariants (raw units):
* `amount_in_net = amount_in − transfer_fee_in`
* `fee_amount = ceil(amount_in_net · effective_fee_rate / 1e6)`;
`protocol_fee_amount` (ceil at `protocol_fee_rate`) and
`creator_fee_amount` (floor of the rest at `creator_fee_bps`) are its
split, the LPs keep the remainder in the reserves
* `in_after.virtual = in_before.virtual + amount_in_net −
protocol_fee_amount − creator_fee_amount` (same delta on `actual`)
* `amount_out_gross` = curve output; `out_after.virtual =
out_before.virtual − amount_out_gross` (same delta on `actual`)
* `amount_out = amount_out_gross − surge_fee_amount` left the vault to
the user, who was credited `amount_out − transfer_fee_out`
* `out_after.protocol_fees_owed − out_before.protocol_fees_owed =
surge_protocol_fee_amount`, creator likewise, and the LP remainder of
the surge went to `out_after.surge_fees_owed` (T12)

fields.name: amount_in
docs: Gross user debit (parameter).

fields.name: transfer_fee_in
docs: Token-2022 transfer fee withheld on the input leg.

fields.name: swap_fee_rate
docs: `pool.swap_fee_rate` in force (hundredths of bps).

fields.name: effective_fee_rate
docs: Rate the cascade ran on: `swap_fee_rate` unless a `DYNAMIC_FEE` hook
overrode it (T9, clamped into `[hook_fee_min, hook_fee_max]`).

fields.name: protocol_fee_rate
docs: `pool.protocol_fee_rate` in force (bps).

fields.name: creator_fee_bps
docs: `pool.creator_fee_bps` in force (bps).

fields.name: fee_amount
docs: Total base swap fee (token_in).

fields.name: amount_out_gross
docs: Curve output (token_out) — what left the trading reserves.

fields.name: surge_fee_amount
docs: Variable sell-off surge fee, total (token_out); 0 without a cap.

fields.name: amount_out
docs: Vault debit to the user: `amount_out_gross − surge_fee_amount`.

fields.name: transfer_fee_out
docs: Token-2022 transfer fee withheld on the output leg.

fields.name: selloff_window
docs: The input token's sell-off window as advanced by this swap; `None`
when the token has no cap. Last on purpose: every field before it has
a fixed Borsh offset (1 tag byte + 56 B when `Some`).

types.name: TokenChange
docs: Single change entry: "I believe slot `index` currently holds
`expected_current`; set it to `new_value`".
`expected_current` is a compare-and-swap guard, not decoration. The
manager computes `new_value` off-chain against whatever it last observed,
then submits a transaction that lands some slots later. Without the
guard the write is unconditional, so any swap or liquidity operation that
landed in between is silently reset — and that window is a property of
Solana's read-then-submit latency, not of operator care, so a careful
manager cannot avoid it. Anyone able to time a swap into the gap can have
its price effect erased.
